references.text: Gideon earlier threatened the men of Succoth with punishment using thorns and briers from the wilderness, and here he fulfills that threat.
The book of Moses describes punishment by beating, which parallels Gideon's use of thorns and briers to discipline the men of Succoth.
Proverbs mentions a rod as discipline for a fool, reflecting Gideon's action of teaching the men of Succoth a lesson through physical punishment.
The young man wrote down the names of the leaders and elders of Succoth, whom Gideon now punishes in this verse.
